Thanks for the details—super helpful. I’m not seeing a widespread Verizon outage in 94103 right now, so this likely points to a line provisioning or device/eSIM issue. Try these steps in order (you can stop when service returns):

Quick recoveries
1) Airplane Mode: On for 60 seconds, then off.
2) Toggle your line: Settings > Cellular > your Verizon line > Turn On This Line OFF, wait 10 seconds, then ON.
3) Network Selection: Settings > Cellular > Network Selection > Automatic ON.
4) Carrier settings: Settings > General > About. If you see “Carrier Settings Update,” tap Update.
5) Force LTE: Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options > Voice & Data > set to LTE or 5G Auto (avoid 5G On for now). Test.

If still “No Service”
6) Try outdoors or a different block (SoMa buildings can be tricky for signal). See if it changes to 1–2 bars or LTE.
7) Enable Wi‑Fi Calling (for temporary calling): Settings > Cellular > Wi‑Fi Calling > On.

Reset and re-provision
8) Reset Network Settings: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings. Note: this erases saved Wi‑Fi/VPN settings.
9) Reinstall your Verizon eSIM:
   - Make sure you have Wi‑Fi and your My Verizon login.
   - Save your EID/IMEI: Settings > General > About.
   - Delete eSIM: Settings > Cellular > your Verizon line > Delete eSIM.
   - Re-add via My Verizon app: Devices > your iPhone > Manage/Activate eSIM > follow prompts; or Settings > Cellular > Add eSIM and follow the Verizon flow.

   - If available, use the “Reset network/refresh” option for the line.

- Re-provision your line/eSIM and push a fresh activation.
- Check for location-based blocks or a routing issue on your number.
- Verify the IMEI isn’t flagged and that your line has correct 5G/LTE features enabled.

A couple of quick questions to help narrow it further:
- Are you seeing any message under Settings > Cellular > your line (e.g., “Activation Required” or “SIM Failure”)?
- Under Settings > General > About, what “Network Provider”/carrier version do you see (e.g., Verizon 56.x)?
- Does moving a few blocks or going outdoors change anything?

Send me what happens after steps 1–5, and I’ll tailor next steps.

Here’s what I found after trying steps 1–5:

- Airplane mode and toggling the line didn’t help—still “No Service.”
- Network selection is set to Automatic.
- No carrier settings update was available.
- Switching to LTE didn’t change anything.

Under Settings > Cellular > my Verizon line, it just says “No Service”—no activation or SIM error messages. In Settings > General > About, the Network Provider is listed as “Verizon 56.0.”

I also tried stepping outside, but there’s still no signal. What should I try next?

Thanks for checking those. Given “No Service” with no SIM/activation errors and no local outage, the next most likely causes are a stuck network profile or a problem with your eSIM/line provisioning. Here’s the fastest way to isolate and fix it:

Do these in order

1) Enable Wi‑Fi Calling (quick workaround)
- Settings > Cellular > Wi‑Fi Calling > On. If it turns on and you can make a call over Wi‑Fi, your line is at least partially provisioned.

2) Reset Network Settings
- Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings.
- This clears saved Wi‑Fi/VPN and reboots radio services. After reboot, re-test in the same spot.

3) Reinstall the Verizon eSIM (fresh provisioning)
- Make sure you’re on Wi‑Fi and have your My Verizon login.
- Note your EID/IMEI: Settings > General > About (optional).
- Delete the eSIM: Settings > Cellular > your Verizon line > Delete eSIM.
- Add it back:
  - Best: My Verizon app > Devices > your iPhone > Manage/Activate eSIM and follow prompts, or
  - Settings > Cellular > Add eSIM > follow the Verizon activation flow.
- Restart if not prompted, then test.

4) Quick account checks in My Verizon
- Confirm your line shows Active (not suspended/blocked) and that the device/IMEI matches your iPhone 14.
- If available, run the “Reset/Refresh network” or “Troubleshoot” tool for your line.
- Verify there’s no past‑due or fraud hold.

If still No Service after eSIM reinstall

5) Cross-test to pinpoint device vs. line
- Move your Verizon eSIM to another unlocked iPhone temporarily (friend/family) via My Verizon. If it works there, your iPhone likely has a device-side issue.
- Or, add any other working Verizon SIM/eSIM to your iPhone. If that line shows service, your phone hardware is fine and your line needs Verizon reprovisioning.
- If neither SIM works in your phone and your eSIM works in another phone, contact Apple Support for a cellular hardware/radio check.

When contacting Verizon, ask them to:
- Fully reprovision your line and push a fresh eSIM activation.
- Clear and rebuild your profile (HSS/UDM) and reset your network registration.
- Verify your features (VoLTE/5G/LTE) and confirm your IMEI/EID are correctly associated.

Send me the results after:
- Reset Network Settings, and
- The eSIM delete/re-add.
If you prefer, we can jump straight to the eSIM reinstall now since you’ve already tried the basics.

Make sure you have reliable Wi‑Fi and a way to receive any Verizon/My Verizon verification codes that isn’t SMS to this phone (email, another phone, or an authenticator).

Prep (2–3 minutes)
- Connect to a stable Wi‑Fi network.
- Have your My Verizon username/password ready and confirm you can complete 2FA without SMS to this phone.
- Note your device identifiers (optional, but helpful if asked):
  - Settings > General > About > EID, IMEI (IMEI2 is typically used for eSIM on iPhone 14). You can screenshot this page.
- Turn off any VPN on the phone. Keep Low Power Mode off.

Part A — Remove the current eSIM
1) Go to Settings > Cellular.
2) Tap your Verizon line.
3) Tap Delete eSIM (or Remove eSIM) and confirm.
4) Wait 15–30 seconds. Your cellular section should no longer list the Verizon plan.

Part B — Add the eSIM back (best method: My Verizon app)
1) On Wi‑Fi, open the My Verizon app and sign in.
2) Go to Account > Devices > select your iPhone > Manage eSIM or Activate/Replace SIM.
   - Wording varies: look for Activate eSIM, Replace SIM, or Switch or Add device on this phone.
3) Select your line and choose to activate on This device.
4) Follow the prompts. If asked, enter or confirm your EID/IMEI. Accept the 911 address/terms.
5) When iOS shows “Finish Setting Up Cellular” or “Cellular Plan Ready to Be Installed,” tap Continue and allow it to download/activate.

  - If you see “Cellular Plan Ready to Be Installed,” tap it and follow prompts, or

- Network Selection = Automatic. Voice & Data = 5G Auto (or LTE if you prefer to test).

- If it keeps failing, in My Verizon run any “Reset/Refresh network” or “Troubleshoot” option for the line, then try activation again.

Would you like me to stay with you as you go through Part A and Part B? If you see any specific error messages or codes, send them here and I’ll adjust the next steps.

I’ll jump on it as soon as you post an update.

I mean the most recent message I sent. My identifier is not available—can you still help me find the content?

I can help, but I need at least one piece of identifying info to safely locate your message without pulling in other people’s data.

Any one of these will work:
- The phone number you sent from (preferred), or your sender_person_id.
- The message_id (if you have it).
- The recipient’s phone number or person ID plus an approximate send time (e.g., “around 2:35 PM today”) or a distinctive keyword/phrase from the message.

If you’re not sure where to find these:
- Phone number: check your app/account settings or your device’s phone number.
- Recipient details: open the conversation thread and copy the contact/number.
- Approximate time: look at your Sent folder or conversation timestamp.
- Message_id: sometimes shown in message details/info within the app.

Once you share any one of the above, I’ll fetch the most recent message you sent and provide its content. If none of these are available, your best next step is to check your device’s Sent/Outbox or contact your workspace admin to retrieve your account identifier.
I don’t have any of those identifiers available. Is there any way you can still retrieve the content of my most recent sent message?

Without any of these, I’d risk pulling other people’s messages, which I can’t do.

Fast ways to get a minimal piece of info:
- Your phone number
  - iPhone: Settings > Phone > My Number
  - Android: Settings > About phone (or About device) > Phone number; if “Unknown,” check Settings > About phone > Status > SIM status
